item.title: Combinatorial group testing for efficient scaling across biological applications
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77055-5

Combinatorial group testing can reduce experimental costs but remains challenging to apply due to its complexity and the lack of implementation tools. Here, the authors present PoolPy, a complete combinatorial group testing framework, enabling up to 93% cost reduction across biological assays.

item.title: Redox-stratified macromolecule degradation supports microbial survival in the oligotrophic Kermadec Trench sediments
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77249-x

Understanding how microbes survive in the crushing pressure and nutrient-poor conditions of the deepest ocean has remained a major challenge. This study reveals that Kermadec Trench microbes thrive by recycling organic matter and flexibly switching energy-generation pathways.

item.title: Unc-51 like kinase 3 (ULK3) contributes to autophagy and cell survival in multiple myeloma
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76711-0

Autophagy-related mechanisms in multiple myeloma (MM) remains to be understood. Here the authors find that ULK3 contributes to autophagy and supports MM cell survival, calling for future development of more selective ULK3-directed therapies.

item.title: Dual-phase engineering of CF<sub>x</sub> electrode and interphase enables low-temperature Li||CF<sub>x</sub> batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76513-4

Li||CFx batteries exhibit severe low-temperature degradation owing to insulating CFx electrodes and sluggish Li+ kinetics. The authors propose a dual-modification strategy combining carbon-coated porous CFx cathodes with an electrolyte-derived interphase, which accelerates Li+ transport and boosts performance at low temperatures.

item.title: Quantifying replication fidelity of unnatural base pairs using nanopore sequencing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76964-9

Expanded DNA alphabets with more than 4 letters can be replicated by polymerases, but with higher error rates than standard DNA. Here the authors develop a high-throughput sequencing approach to quantify the replication fidelity of unnatural base pairs.

item.title: BRANCHED1 acts as a rheostat of Nuclear Factor Y-dependent epigenetic regulation in axillary bud development
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77029-7

Shoot branching plasticity is largely regulated by BRC1. The authors show that BRC1 acts as a dose-dependent rheostat, modulating NF-Y-mediated chromatin looping and H3K27me3 demethylation at floral organ development genes to fine-tune axillary bud activity.

item.title: Protein entanglement misfolding influences whether proteins undergo proteasomal degradation or persist in near-native misfolded states
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76875-9

Protein entanglements can generate long-lived misfolded states, but their cellular fate is poorly understood. Here, the authors combine proteomics and simulations to show that entanglement misfolding promotes proteasomal degradation, while soluble, near-native misfolded proteins escape degradation.

item.title: Ectoderm tensile stress controls mesoderm internalization during embryo gastrulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77010-4

The biomechanical basis for tissue folding during morphogenesis remains incompletely understood. Here they show that precisely balanced mechanical tension in tissues surrounding the future mesoderm is essential for its internalization during fruit fly gastrulation.

item.title: Substrate curvature and stiffness equivalence in governing cell mechanosensing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76866-w

This study reveals how cells translate substrate stiffness and curvature into biological responses through focal adhesion tilting, uncovering a mechanical equivalence that opens new routes for designing cell-instructive biomaterials.

item.title: Author Correction: Multimodal analysis of cfDNA methylomes for early detecting esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions

item.title: The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77112-z

The molecular function of many mitochondrial proteins remains unknown. Here, the authors present MitoMatch, an AlphaFold Multimer-based compendium of mitochondrial protein interactions that links orphan proteins to known pathways, defines the CoQ metabolon, and reveals the role of COA4 in copper delivery to cytochrome c oxidase.

item.title: Role of natural halogen chemistry on the evolution of global stratospheric ozone depletion
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76600-6

Halogens from natural sources account for a substantial fraction of stratospheric ozone depletion, contributing up to half of recent lower-stratospheric ozone loss and delaying Antarctic ozone recovery by several decades.

item.title: Homo-metal-element mediated surface modification of sapphire for robust epitaxy of wafer-scale single-crystalline 2D semiconductors
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77131-w

The wafer-scale growth of 2D transition metal dichalcogenides is desired for their electronic applications. Here, the authors report a surface modification strategy of commercial sapphire substrates to grow wafer-scale monolayer WS2 or MoS2 single crystals, showing their application for high-performance transistors arrays.
